causes.evidence: Pricing stayed at 1pp, the same as January–March. Later CPI would imply 5.41pp in the frozen model.
causes.interpretation: The US price proxy and long-history relationship overpredicted global company pricing.
causes.status: Model failure demonstrated; exact commercial attribution unavailable

causes.evidence: Hair and personal care grew, while China skin-care volume declined.
causes.interpretation: Carrying the prior +5% volume forward missed a changing category / geographic mix.
causes.status: Reported category explanation; no exact two-point allocation

causes.evidence: Reported 3pp volume plus 1pp pricing; market-data replacement adds only 0.05pp to the model.
causes.interpretation: Most of the 0.71pp miss remains in the company–market relationship.
causes.status: Arithmetic diagnosis; residual is not identified causality

causes.evidence: Baby improved in China; feminine-care volume weakened in Europe; family care had weaker volume and promotions.
causes.interpretation: The segment combines businesses moving in different directions; the net miss is 0.65pp.

causes.evidence: Fabric-care volume grew, led by Europe; home-care volume declined, mainly North America.
causes.interpretation: The four-quarter average missed a modest net improvement.
causes.status: Reported category divergence; no country dollar split

causes.evidence: Pricing remained 2pp; oral-care volume declined while personal health had stronger pricing and volume.
causes.interpretation: The model expected more pricing than the company realized; weak volume is a separate issue.
